neighbours.label: the halogen piece inside a compound chemical name, predicting '-alide'/'-chlor-' (silver-h|alide, organo|h|alide, hypo|ch|lorite, tetr|achloride)
fire: Black-and-white paper is coated with a silver-halide emulsion that darkens in light.
Bacteria in the aquifer slowly broke down the organohalide contaminants.
The cleaner listed calcium hypochlorite as its main active ingredient.
Older dry-cleaning shops relied on carbon tetrachloride as a solvent.
Microbes that degrade organohalides are useful for cleaning polluted soil.
Each frame of film holds millions of tiny silver-halide crystals.
Pool owners often add sodium hypochlorite once a week.
The refinery converts the ore into pure titanium tetrachloride first.
quiet: Black-and-white paper is coated with a gelatin emulsion that darkens in light.
Bacteria in the aquifer slowly broke down the petroleum contaminants.
The cleaner listed sodium carbonate as its main active ingredient.
Older dry-cleaning shops relied on petroleum naphtha as a solvent.
Microbes that degrade hydrocarbons are useful for cleaning polluted soil.
Each frame of film holds millions of tiny dye-forming crystals.
Pool owners often add sodium bicarbonate once a week.
The refinery converts the ore into pure titanium dioxide first.

notes: Card top examples are silver-halide, organohalide, tetrachloride, thermohaline. Probe: the hyphenated/fused compound fires, 'silver halide' with a space and lowercase ' chlorine' do not.
